Download fire hotspot data from INPE's Programa Queimadas

Source: R/inpe.R
download_firespots.Rd

Downloads the annual records of fire hotspots (*focos de queimada*) detected by satellite over Brazil, made available by the National Institute for Space Research (INPE) through the *Programa Queimadas*. The files include detections from all satellites monitored by INPE.

Usage

download_firespots(years = 2025, dest_dir = NULL)

Arguments

years

Integer vector specifying the years to download. Historical data are available from 1998 onwards. The default is `2025`.

dest_dir

Character. Directory where the extracted CSV files are saved (e.g. `"./data/raw/"`). It is created if it does not exist. If `NULL` (default), files are extracted to a temporary directory and discarded at the end of the R session.

Value

A data frame with one row per fire hotspot, combining all requested `years`.

Details

For each year, a ZIP file is downloaded from INPE's open data server (<https://data.inpe.br/queimadas/portal/dados-abertos/>), extracted into `dest_dir` (or a temporary directory) and read with [data.table::fread()]. The yearly tables are then stacked into a single data frame.

When `dest_dir` is set, years whose CSV (`focos_br_todos-sats_year.csv`) already exists in `dest_dir` are read from disk instead of being downloaded again, so an internet connection is only required for missing years. A message lists the years that are read from disk.

Column names are kept as distributed by the source. The main columns are the hotspot coordinates (`latitude`, `longitude`), the detection time (`data_pas`), the satellite (`satelite`), the location (`pais`, `estado`, `municipio`, `bioma`), and fire-related indicators such as `numero_dias_sem_chuva`, `precipitacao`, `risco_fogo` and `frp` (fire radiative power). The files do not include IBGE municipality codes; to link hotspots to [municipality] or [mun_stations], use the coordinates (e.g. a spatial join with municipality boundaries) or the municipality and state names.

Although records are available since 1998, the structure of the files has changed over time: newer years may include columns that do not exist in older ones, and column names or types may differ. When several years are requested, tables are combined with [dplyr::bind_rows()], so columns missing in a given year are filled with `NA`, and incompatible column types across years may raise an error. The columns described above refer to recent years; check the data before combining long periods.

See also

[download_disasters()], [municipality], [mun_stations]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

## Download a single year
firespots <- download_firespots(years = 2024)

## Download multiple years
firespots <- download_firespots(years = 2022:2024)

## Keep the CSV files locally
firespots <- download_firespots(years = 2024, dest_dir = "./data/raw/")

} # }
